NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme via periodic dissolved-gas analysis sampling. Our same-class mechanism departs by using multi-sensor fusion of existing parameters to infer early fault development through thermal-electrical interaction patterns. The failure-physics connection is that partial discharges and thermal faults create distinct thermal-electrical signatures that deviate from normal operating relationships before gas generation becomes significant.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the Arrhenius equation for thermal aging: Rate = A·exp(-Ea/RT), where temperature exponentially accelerates fault development. For a 40 MVA transformer, a 10°C temperature increase approximately doubles the aging rate. Our indicator detects sustained thermal excursions above normal operating relationships, which precedes gas formation by weeks. CALCULATED: A 15% sustained deviation in the thermal model would correspond to approximately 30 days of accelerated aging per IEEE C57.91.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
1. Data acquisition system (existing transformer monitoring system) - same class as standard DGA sampling equipment
2. Signal processing unit (off-the-shelf industrial computer) - same class as existing transformer control systems
3. Thermal model algorithm (software implementation) - uses existing top-oil temperature, load current, ambient temperature inputs
4. Pressure monitoring (existing tank pressure sensor) - same class as existing protection systems
5. Deviation calculation module (software) - computes normalized difference between measured and predicted thermal parameters
6. Time-series analysis module (software) - implements 30-day sliding window to detect sustained deviations

ASSUMPTION: The existing monitoring system has sufficient computational capacity to run the thermal model algorithm. Justification: Modern transformer monitoring systems typically include embedded processors capable of this calculation.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installability: SAME - uses existing sensors and monitoring infrastructure
- Operability: SAME - operates continuously at 15-minute resolution without operator intervention
- Maintenance: SAME - software-based requires no additional maintenance beyond standard system updates
- Cost class: SAME - leverages existing infrastructure with minimal additional software development cost

EXECUTABLE TEST:
PROTOCOL: 
1. Collect historical data from 10 transformers with confirmed incipient faults (partial discharge and thermal) and 10 healthy transformers over 2-year period
2. Implement the predictor algorithm on a test platform
3. Run predictor on historical data with 30-day look-ahead window
4. Measure time-to-detection from first measurable deviation to fault confirmation

INSTRUMENTS:
- Historical data processing system
- Fault confirmation records (DGA, visual inspection, electrical tests)
- Time-series analysis software

PASS/FAIL THRESHOLD: 
- PASS: Predictor flags ≥90% of faults ≥30 days before DGA confirmation
- FAIL: Predictor flags <90% of faults or <30 days before confirmation in more than 10% of cases

DURATION: 4 weeks for historical data processing and analysis

KILL CRITERION: If false positive rate exceeds 5% (indicating normal operation flagged as fault) or detection sensitivity falls below 90%
